page: Microsoft Azure E128-64s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. This server does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on remote Premium Storage options.

In benchmark evaluations, the E128-64s_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and top-tier memory performance. While single-core stress-ng and compression tasks register as average, multi-core performance is strong, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 76,622.09 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 407.23 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching top-tier speeds of 391.59 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 171.9 GB/sec for write operations. Database operations are highly efficient, with PassMark database benchmarks scoring in the top tier at 35,230.63 and Redis SET operations achieving 85.44 million operations per second. Additionally, the server exhibits top-tier static web serving throughput at 94.28 GB/sec and strong performance in medium-model (7B) LLM inference.

The qualitative cost profile of the E128-64s_v6 reflects its high resource density, particularly its massive 1 TB memory allocation relative to the 64 vCPUs. This configuration offers high cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage but benefit from high memory bandwidth and dedicated compute resources. The absence of local storage and GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, positioning this instance specifically for workloads dependent on external storage networks. It is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
